description: We are a Maryland-based parent-and-child creative duo combining early-childhood imagination with real NASA space science. Inspired by a toddler's curiosity about bees and space explorers, AstroHive Explorers MD builds interactive, multi-generational storytelling experiences that bring NASA's retired Moon and Mars missions to life for young learners and families.
summary: AstroHive Explorers MD developed Buzzy AstroWing's Space Mission, an interactive, read-aloud web storybook and NASA Ghost Rover field guide for the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge. Following Buzzy AstroWing, a curious "Space Bee" visiting retired NASA spacecraft on the Moon and Mars, the app features a dual-layer Family Co-Play Mode for toddlers, kids, and parents. Toddlers explore with giant shape-and-color tap targets, read-aloud narration, and original sing-along melodies, while older learners interact with real NASA telemetry—clearing Opportunity’s 2018 dust storm, triggering InSight’s marsquakes, and testing Earth-to-Mars radio delays. Built using verified NASA archives for Apollo 15, Opportunity, InSight, and Apollo 12’s Surveyor 3 visit, the app concludes by inviting families to join NASA’s "Soar with Dragonfly" campaign—showing how preserving past space archaeology inspires the next generation of explorers.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Buzzy AstroWing's Space Mission is an interactive, read-aloud web storybook and NASA Ghost Rover field guide built for the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge. Players follow "Buzzy," a curious Space Bee flying ahead of future astronauts to visit retired NASA spacecraft resting on the Moon and Mars.

Using an intentional Family Co-Play Mode toggle, the app adapts seamlessly to different age levels on both mobile and desktop screens:

  • Toddler Play Layer (Zero Reading Required): Features large, glowing shape-and-color tap targets (Yellow Circle Wheel, Gold Square Camera, Red Dust Cloud, Orange Quake Circle), built-in read-aloud narration, zero timers or fail states, and two original sing-along melodies ("Buzzing Through the Stars" and "Dusty Rover Lullaby").
  • Junior Astronaut Telemetry Layer: Turns real NASA mission data into hands-on mini-simulations. Users swipe away the June 2018 global dust storm to watch Opportunity’s solar power recover from 22 Watt-Hours to 900 Watt-Hours, trigger InSight’s Sol 1222 Magnitude 5 marsquake, and compare light-speed radio delays from Earth to the Moon (1.3 seconds) versus Mars (~12 minutes).
  • Real NASA Vision & Space Archaeology: One-click toggles reveal authentic NASA mission photography, exact landing coordinates, astronaut and Principal Investigator credits, and the real-world history of Apollo 12 astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean visiting Surveyor 3 on the Moon in 1969 to study how space hardware ages.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Early STEM Accessibility: Bridges the gap between complex planetary telemetry and early childhood education, allowing toddlers, older siblings, and parents to learn together on the same screen.
  • Preserving Space Heritage: Honors the engineers, scientists, and astronauts behind historic missions—including Apollo 15, Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity (MER-B), InSight, and Surveyor 3—ensuring their discoveries and hardware are remembered rather than forgotten.
  • Future Vision & Next Steps: Serves as a Hackathon Preview Edition designed to expand into a full 32-page illustrated print and sing-along children's book that introduces young learners and families to space heritage and space archaeology. To show young explorers how lessons from retired Moon and Mars hardware shape future missions, our final screen also connects families with NASA’s upcoming Dragonfly rotorcraft to Titan (built in Laurel, Maryland)—inviting parents and kids to click through to NASA’s "Soar with Dragonfly" campaign to claim a free boarding pass and send their names to Titan.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Web Technologies & APIs: Built as a self-contained interactive web application using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, layered custom SVG illustrations, touch/swipe gesture controls, the Web Speech API for read-aloud narration, and the Web Audio API for real-time sound synthesis and original music playback.
  • Development & Hosting Platform: Developed and deployed publicly using Replit (including Replit's AI Coding Assistant for code generation, custom SVG graphics, and audio synthesis).
  • Official Data Sources: Verified mission coordinates, telemetry figures, and crew/team credits against NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) and NASA JPL mission archives.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered

  • Dual-Layer Intergenerational Design: Most educational space apps target either adults/students with dense data or young kids with purely fictional cartoons. We creatively merged both into one screen so a toddler can tap shapes and sing along while a parent or older sibling explores authentic NASA telemetry and coordinates.
  • Child Privacy & Safety (COPPA Compliance): Designed from the ground up with zero user tracking, zero external data collection, and no account logins required, ensuring a completely safe environment for young learners.
  • Scientific & Human Accuracy: Beyond listing spacecraft names, we intentionally credited the real people behind the hardware—such as Apollo 15 astronauts David R. Scott, James B. Irwin, and Alfred M. Worden; NASA MSFC’s Saverio "Sonny" Morea; Opportunity PI Dr. Steve Squyres; and InSight PI Dr. Bruce Banerdt and Deputy PI Dr. Suzanne Smrekar—to show young explorers that human teamwork drives space discovery.
